names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 18 iunie, «Sfântul Cuvios Leontie Dionisiatul, Izvorâtorul de mir».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 18 Ιουνίου, «Όσιος Λεόντιος ο Αθωνίτης ο Μυροβλήτης», with the rank word and the epithets left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 18. јун ст. ст., „Преподобни Леонтије прозорљиви“ — Преподобни is the rank and comes off, and what is left is the forename **with its by-name kept**: прозорљиви, clear-sighted, which is not a rank in this corpus’s vocabulary and is therefore part of the name the heading gives. Keeping it is what makes this form clear: `foldchk.py` returns NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM for «Леонтије прозорљиви», where for the bare «Леонтије» it returns `leontius-24-april` and `leontius-of-arabia` — and the same day’s first entry writes that bare form, so stripping the by-name here would have folded two folders of one day together. The Myrrh-gusher and the Athonite of the other books’ forms are not in this heading and are not built onto it.

birth.note: saint.gr: «Γεννήθηκε το 1520 μ.Χ. στο Άργος της Πελοποννήσου σύμφωνα με τον Άγιο Νικόδημο τον Αγιορείτη και την παράδοση των πατέρων της Ιεράς Μονής Διονυσίου», with its page head «(1520 - 1605)». doxologia gave no birth year.

death.note: doxologia.ro: «Cuviosul Leontie și-a cunoscut dinainte sfârșitul și a adormit cu pace, după o scurtă boală, în ziua de 16 martie 1605»; the same page has him entering Dionysiou «în 1537» and struggling there sixty-eight years. saint.gr agrees on the year: «Ο όσιος Λεόντιος απεβίωσε το 1605 μ.Χ. σε ηλικία 85 ετών», but has him sixty years in the monastery, not sixty-eight.

attestations.note: Not checked: days.pravoslavie.ru for the corresponding Julian day (24 September 2026).

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 18 iunie — «Sfântul Cuvios Leontie Dionisiatul, Izvorâtorul de mir»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 18ης Ιουνίου — «Όσιος Λεόντιος ο Αθωνίτης ο Μυροβλήτης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 18 Ιουνίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. It is plainly the same monk: the myrrh-gushing Leontius of the monastery of Saint Dionysius on Athos, born at Argos, dead in 1605, whom the folder's Romanian row already keeps on 18 June. saint.gr adds the birth year 1520, the age of eighty-five, the manuscript its Life survives in, the prophecy about Nauplion, and a relic at the monastery of Zerbitsa near Sparta; it has him sixty years in the monastery where doxologia has sixty-eight, which is recorded in the life and not resolved here. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the life page.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 01.07.2026 (18. јун ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Леонтије прозорљиви“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. The Julian 18 June is the same menologion number this folder’s Romanian and Greek rows carry, so there is no second day and no §4 note is owed. TWO ENTRIES, TWO LEONTIUSES, AND THE BY-NAME RULE DOING THE WORK. This day prints a `Свети мученик Леонтије` and a `Преподобни Леонтије прозорљиви`, two different men, and both have folders. Stripped to the bare forename both would store the same `sr` string and the day would have folded two of its own folders together. **The second heading gives a by-name and it is kept**, so the forms written are «Леонтије» and «Леонтије прозорљиви», and only the first takes a fold. `dates` LEFT AS THEY STOOD, AND A THIRD BOOK BREAKING A TIE. The folder holds `death` 1605 `attested` off doxologia’s «a adormit cu pace … în ziua de 16 martie 1605» and `birth` 1520 `traditional` off saint.gr. This book states the death year flat — „преставио се 1605. године“ — so there is nothing to widen and nothing to choose, and `dates` is not touched. **But it does settle something the folder recorded as a disagreement**: doxologia had him enter Dionysiou in 1537 and struggle there sixty-eight years, saint.gr had him sixty years in the monastery, and the folder’s own `death` note says so. This book says „подвизавао се у манастиру Дионисијату шездесет година“ — sixty years — **and says it twice**, the second time in the sentence about going in and coming out, „за пуних шездесет година“. So two of three books now read sixty. That is written into the life and **not into `dates`**, because a duration is not a year and the field the arithmetic would reach is a `birth` this folder already holds off another book. **NO `birth` IS TOUCHED AND THE EIGHTY-FIVE YEARS ARE REFUSED**: „будући осамдесет пет година од рођења“ is a lifespan, and sixteen hundred and five less eighty-five is a year reached by arithmetic — both refused on their own, and refused twice over because saint.gr’s own 1520 is that same subtraction made by somebody else and is the folder’s, not mine to endorse or to move. THE ONE THING THIS BOOK HAS THAT NEITHER OTHER BOOK HAS. „Само једном ушао у манастир и само једном изишао из манастира за пуних шездесет година“ — in sixty full years he went into the monastery once and came out of it once: in when he first entered Dionysiou, out when they carried him out dead to bury him. Nothing of that is in either of the other two lives, and it is the whole reason this row is worth the paragraph. WHAT IT AGREES ON. „Пореклом Грк из Пелопонеза“ — a Greek of the Peloponnese by origin, where saint.gr named Argos in the Peloponnese; **the wider reading is written and the narrower left standing**. „Имао је чудесан дар прозорљивости и прорицања“ — the wonderful gift of clear sight and of foretelling; and „по смрти из његових моштију потекло је миро“, that myrrh flowed from his relics after his death, which is the Myrrh-gusher of the display name and is already in the folder. `types` UNTOUCHED, AND **`прозорљиви` GIVES NO TYPE**. `venerable`, `hermit` and `wonderworker` are all there; Преподобни is the `venerable` and the heading’s one other word, прозорљиви, means clear-sighted, for which **there is no word in the vocabulary at all** — so it goes into the name form, where it breaks a fold, and into the life, and nowhere else. No `office`, no `locations`: the Peloponnese and the monastery are the folder’s already and unbounded. NO ROWS: the entry names no person but him. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

hymns.text: Τοῦ Ἄργους ἀγλάισμα, οἷά περ γόνος κλεινὸς καὶ θεῖον γεώργιον τῆς τοῦ Προδρόμου Μονῆς ἐδείχθης Λεόντιε. Σὺ γὰρ δι᾽ ἐνάρετου πολιτείας ἐκλάμψας, ὤφθης Χριστοῦ θεράπων καὶ σεπτὸς μυροβλύτης, διὸ σὲ Πάτερ συμφώνως πάντες γεραίρομεν.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, ᾌχος δ´, Ταχὺ προκατάλαβε — on the page of «Όσιος Λεόντιος ο Αθωνίτης ο Μυροβλήτης», and it names him and Argos

english.text: Splendour of Argos, as her renowned offspring and as a divine husbandry of the monastery of the Forerunner wast thou shown to be, Leontius. For having shone by a virtuous life, thou wast seen to be a servant of Christ and a venerable gusher of myrrh; therefore we all with one voice honour thee, father.

hymns.text: Τῷ Σωτῆρι Ὄσιε ἀκολουθήσας ὁσίως, σεαυτὸν καθήγνισας δι᾽ ἀρετῶν ἐμμελείας· ὅθεν σε ὁ Ζωοδότης Λόγος δοξάσας, ἔδειξε πηγὴν τὸ σκῆνός σου θείου μύρου· διὰ τοῦτο σοὶ βοῶμεν· χαῖροις θεόφρον πάτερ Λεόντιε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, ᾌχος γ´, Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον — on the same page, and it names him and the myrrh

english.text: Having followed the Saviour in holiness, venerable one, thou didst purify thyself by the harmony of the virtues; wherefore the Word, the Giver of life, glorifying thee, made thy body a fountain of divine myrrh. Therefore we cry to thee: rejoice, God-minded father Leontius.
